title: CTS Christian Education — Unit 5: The Learning Environment

blocks.en: Christian Education — Unit 5: The Learning Environment
blocks.es_reference: Educación Cristiana — Unidad 5: El Ambiente de Aprendizaje

blocks.en: Andi turns from the learners to the place where the learning happens. A skilled teacher and a willing learner can still be defeated by a poor environment. This unit prepares the field.
blocks.es_reference: Andi se vuelve de los aprendices al lugar donde sucede el aprendizaje. Un maestro hábil y un aprendiz dispuesto aún pueden ser derrotados por un ambiente pobre. Esta unidad prepara el campo.

blocks.en: Unit 5 · Mark 14:15 · The Place
blocks.es_reference: Unidad 5 · Marcos 14:15 · El Lugar

blocks.en: The Learning Environment
blocks.es_reference: El Ambiente de Aprendizaje

blocks.en: "A large upper room furnished and prepared..."
blocks.es_reference: «Un gran aposento alto, dispuesto...»

blocks.en: Unit Scripture: "Then he will show you a large upper room, furnished and prepared; there make ready for us." — Mark 14:15 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Escritura de la Unidad: «Y él os mostrará un gran aposento alto ya dispuesto; preparad para nosotros allí». — Marcos 14:15 (RVG)

blocks.en: Orientation: A Field Prepared, or a Field Lost
blocks.es_reference: Orientación: Un campo preparado, o un campo perdido

blocks.en: A teacher can be brilliant, and a learner can be hungry, and still nothing happens, because the environment defeats them both. We have all sat through that experience. The teacher knew the material. The learner wanted to learn. But the air conditioning was broken, the chairs were the wrong size, the hallway noise drowned out every sentence, the hour was wrong, the mood was tired. Whatever the cause, the seed never reached the soil because the field itself was unprepared.
blocks.es_reference: Un maestro puede ser brillante, y un aprendiz puede estar hambriento, y aun así nada sucede, porque el ambiente los derrota a ambos. Todos hemos pasado por esa experiencia. El maestro conocía el material. El aprendiz quería aprender. Pero el aire acondicionado estaba descompuesto, las sillas eran del tamaño equivocado, el ruido del pasillo ahogaba cada oración, la hora era equivocada, el ánimo estaba cansado. Cualquiera que fuera la causa, la semilla nunca alcanzó la tierra porque el campo mismo estaba sin preparar.

blocks.en: This unit is about preparing the field. Three environments wrap around every Christian Education classroom. The first is the physical environment — the room itself. The second is the emotional environment — the atmosphere among the learners. The third is the spiritual environment — the presence of God in the room. The teacher who attends to all three is the teacher whose lesson plan has somewhere to land. The teacher who attends to none of them is the teacher who blames the lesson plan when the lesson fails.
blocks.es_reference: Esta unidad trata de preparar el campo. Tres ambientes envuelven cada aula de Educación Cristiana. El primero es el ambiente físico — el cuarto mismo. El segundo es el ambiente emocional — la atmósfera entre los aprendices. El tercero es el ambiente espiritual — la presencia de Dios en el cuarto. El maestro que atiende los tres es el maestro cuyo plan de lección tiene dónde caer. El maestro que no atiende ninguno es el maestro que culpa al plan de lección cuando la lección falla.

blocks.en: A skilled teacher and a willing learner can still be defeated by a poor environment.
blocks.es_reference: Un maestro hábil y un aprendiz dispuesto aún pueden ser derrotados por un ambiente pobre.

blocks.en: The Master Teacher Himself sent two disciples ahead to prepare the room where the most important teaching meal in history would be eaten. "He will show you a large upper room, furnished and prepared; there make ready for us" (Mark 14:15). If Jesus prepared the room before he taught in it, the Christian Education teacher prepares the room.
blocks.es_reference: El Maestro de Maestros mismo envió a dos discípulos por adelantado a preparar el cuarto donde se comería la comida de enseñanza más importante en la historia. «Y él os mostrará un gran aposento alto ya dispuesto; preparad para nosotros allí» (Marcos 14:15). Si Jesús preparó el cuarto antes de enseñar en él, el maestro de Educación Cristiana prepara el cuarto.

blocks.en: I. The Physical Place: The Boat as Pulpit
blocks.es_reference: I. El lugar físico: La barca como púlpito

blocks.en: Mark 4 records one of the simplest examples of a master teacher choosing his physical environment. The crowd had grown so large on the shore of Galilee that Jesus could no longer be heard or seen by everyone. "And he began again to teach by the sea side: and there was gathered unto him a great multitude, so that he entered into a ship, and sat in the sea; and the whole multitude was by the sea on the land" (Mark 4:1). The lake itself became a natural amphitheater. The water carried his voice. Every face in the crowd had a clear view. The fishermen who heard him preach the parable of the sower that day heard it in conditions optimized by the teacher himself.
blocks.es_reference: Marcos 4 registra uno de los ejemplos más simples de un maestro de maestros escogiendo su ambiente físico. La multitud había crecido tanto en la orilla de Galilea que Jesús ya no podía ser oído o visto por todos. «Y otra vez comenzó a enseñar junto al mar, y se reunió alrededor de Él una gran multitud, tanto, que entró en una barca, y se sentó en el mar; y toda la multitud estaba en tierra junto al mar» (Marcos 4:1). El lago mismo se convirtió en un anfiteatro natural. El agua llevó su voz. Cada rostro en la multitud tuvo una vista clara. Los pescadores que lo oyeron predicar la parábola del sembrador aquel día la oyeron en condiciones optimizadas por el maestro mismo.

blocks.en: The Christian Education teacher does not have a Sea of Galilee, but he has a room. He has chairs. He has a table or a board or a flannelgraph. He has lighting and temperature and the sound of the air conditioning. Each of these is part of the lesson. The teacher who walks into a cluttered, dim, hot room ten minutes before class and asks the learners to focus on the Word of God is asking them to overcome obstacles he himself put in their way.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro de Educación Cristiana no tiene un Mar de Galilea, pero tiene un cuarto. Tiene sillas. Tiene una mesa o una pizarra o un franelógrafo. Tiene iluminación y temperatura y el sonido del aire acondicionado. Cada uno de estos es parte de la lección. El maestro que entra a un cuarto desordenado, oscuro, y caliente diez minutos antes de la clase y le pide a los aprendices que se enfoquen en la Palabra de Dios les está pidiendo que venzan obstáculos que él mismo puso en su camino.

blocks.en: What does the physical place need? Cleanliness — the room scrubbed before the learners arrive, not after. Brightness — dim rooms produce dim attention. Comfortable temperature — neither stifling nor freezing. Seating that fits the body — a four-year-old in an adult chair is climbing a mountain before the lesson begins. Visibility — every learner should see the teacher and the visual aids without straining. Quiet — distant noises become loud noises in a small room. And supplies ready and within reach — pencils, papers, pictures, whatever the lesson requires, organized on a side table so the lesson is never interrupted by a search through a closet.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Qué necesita el lugar físico? Limpieza — el cuarto restregado antes de que los aprendices lleguen, no después. Luminosidad — los cuartos oscuros producen atención oscura. Temperatura cómoda — ni sofocante ni helada. Asientos que se ajustan al cuerpo — un niño de cuatro años en una silla de adulto está escalando una montaña antes de que la lección comience. Visibilidad — cada aprendiz debe ver al maestro y las ayudas visuales sin esforzarse. Quietud — los ruidos distantes se vuelven ruidos fuertes en un cuarto pequeño. Y materiales listos y al alcance — lápices, papeles, cuadros, lo que la lección requiera, organizado en una mesa lateral para que la lección nunca sea interrumpida por una búsqueda en un armario.

blocks.en: None of this is glamorous. All of it matters. Every minute the teacher invests on Saturday afternoon arranging the room saves five minutes on Sunday morning that should have been spent teaching.
blocks.es_reference: Nada de esto es glamoroso. Todo esto importa. Cada minuto que el maestro invierte el sábado por la tarde arreglando el cuarto le ahorra cinco minutos el domingo por la mañana que deberían haberse gastado enseñando.

blocks.en: II. The Time and Schedule: Paul at the School of Tyrannus
blocks.es_reference: II. El tiempo y el horario: Pablo en la escuela de Tirano

blocks.en: Acts 19 records an unusual line about the apostle Paul's teaching ministry in Ephesus. After three months of preaching in the synagogue, Paul faced opposition and moved his teaching out. "He departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus. And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks" (Acts 19:9–10).
blocks.es_reference: Hechos 19 registra una línea inusual acerca del ministerio de enseñanza del apóstol Pablo en Éfeso. Después de tres meses de predicar en la sinagoga, Pablo enfrentó oposición y movió su enseñanza fuera. «Apartándose de ellos separó a los discípulos, disputando cada día en la escuela de uno llamado Tirano. Y esto fue hecho por espacio de dos años; de manera que todos los que habitaban en Asia, judíos y griegos, oyeron la palabra del Señor Jesús» (Hechos 19:9–10).

blocks.en: Paul rented a hall. He taught daily. He kept it up for two years. None of this is spelled out in Scripture as a command for how every classroom must be run, but notice three things worth learning from the arrangement. First, Paul secured a fixed place. Tyrannus's school was a known address. Anyone who wanted to learn knew where to go. Second, Paul kept a fixed time. Tradition holds that he taught during the heat of the day when the Greek school was closed for siesta — a slot both predictable and protected. Third, Paul kept it up. Same place, same hour, day after day, for twenty-four months. The result: "all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus." One classroom changed a province.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo rentó un salón. Enseñó diariamente. Lo mantuvo por dos años. Nada de esto está establecido en la Escritura como un mandamiento sobre cómo debe funcionar cada aula, pero note tres cosas que vale la pena aprender del arreglo. Primero, Pablo aseguró un lugar fijo. La escuela de Tirano era una dirección conocida. Cualquiera que quisiera aprender sabía adónde ir. Segundo, Pablo mantuvo un tiempo fijo. La tradición sostiene que enseñaba durante el calor del día cuando la escuela griega estaba cerrada por la siesta — un horario predecible y protegido. Tercero, Pablo lo mantuvo. El mismo lugar, la misma hora, día tras día, por veinticuatro meses. El resultado: «todos los que habitaban en Asia... oyeron la palabra del Señor Jesús». Una aula cambió una provincia.

blocks.en: The Christian Education classroom needs the same kind of dependable schedule. The lesson begins on time. The lesson ends on time. The classroom is the same classroom each Sunday, not a moving target. The teacher arrives early, not at the bell. Predictable time is an environment all by itself. Children especially — but adults too — learn faster when they do not have to spend the first ten minutes wondering where the teacher is and whether the class is happening at all.
blocks.es_reference: El aula de Educación Cristiana necesita la misma clase de horario confiable. La lección comienza a tiempo. La lección termina a tiempo. El aula es la misma aula cada domingo, no un blanco móvil. El maestro llega temprano, no al timbre. El tiempo predecible es un ambiente por sí solo. Especialmente los niños — pero también los adultos — aprenden más rápido cuando no tienen que pasar los primeros diez minutos preguntándose dónde está el maestro y si la clase está sucediendo.

blocks.en: A note about the length of class. There is no perfect length. Children need shorter and more varied; adults can sustain longer. The teacher who runs short on material early in the year and runs long on material later in the year is a teacher learning his learners. The schedule should serve the learners, not the lesson plan and not the teacher's preferences.
blocks.es_reference: Una nota sobre la duración de la clase. No hay duración perfecta. Los niños necesitan más corto y más variado; los adultos pueden sostener más largo. El maestro que se queda corto de material temprano en el año y se queda largo de material tarde en el año es un maestro aprendiendo a sus aprendices. El horario debe servir a los aprendices, no al plan de lección y no a las preferencias del maestro.

blocks.en: III. The Atmosphere of Welcome
blocks.es_reference: III. La atmósfera de bienvenida

blocks.en: The room may be perfect. The schedule may be predictable. And the learner may walk out the door and never come back, because the atmosphere was wrong.
blocks.es_reference: El cuarto puede ser perfecto. El horario puede ser predecible. Y el aprendiz puede salir por la puerta y nunca volver, porque la atmósfera estaba mal.

blocks.en: Atmosphere is the hardest environment to define and the most important to preserve. It is the unspoken answer the learner gets to three questions before he sits down: Am I welcome here? Is it safe to ask anything? Will I be valued whether I know the right answer or not?
blocks.es_reference: La atmósfera es el ambiente más difícil de definir y el más importante de preservar. Es la respuesta no hablada que el aprendiz recibe a tres preguntas antes de sentarse: ¿Soy bienvenido aquí? ¿Es seguro preguntar cualquier cosa? ¿Seré valorado independientemente de si sé la respuesta correcta?

blocks.en: If the atmosphere answers yes, the learner will return next week even if the lesson was uneven. If the atmosphere answers no, the learner will not return even if the lesson was excellent. The teacher cannot answer those three questions with a sign on the wall. The teacher answers them with eyes that meet the learner's eyes, with a name spoken at the door, with a question welcomed without an eye-roll, with a wrong answer received without sarcasm, with a slow learner given the same patience as the quick one.
blocks.es_reference: Si la atmósfera responde sí, el aprendiz volverá la próxima semana aun si la lección fue desigual. Si la atmósfera responde no, el aprendiz no volverá aun si la lección fue excelente. El maestro no puede responder esas tres preguntas con un letrero en la pared. El maestro las responde con ojos que se encuentran con los ojos del aprendiz, con un nombre pronunciado en la puerta, con una pregunta recibida sin un rodar de ojos, con una respuesta equivocada recibida sin sarcasmo, con un aprendiz lento recibiendo la misma paciencia que el rápido.

blocks.en: The early church understood this so well that Luke uses one Greek word over and over to describe their gatherings: homothumadon, "with one accord." It means with one mind, in one mood. "And they continued daily with one accord in the temple" (Acts 2:46). "All these continued with one accord in prayer" (Acts 1:14). The believers met with an atmosphere. People walked in from the streets and felt the atmosphere before they ever heard a sermon. "And of the rest durst no man join himself to them: but the people magnified them" (Acts 5:13). Even unbelievers could feel the difference between that room and any other room in Jerusalem.
blocks.es_reference: La iglesia primitiva entendió esto tan bien que Lucas usa una palabra griega una y otra vez para describir sus reuniones: homothumadon, «con un mismo corazón». Significa con una mente, en un mismo ánimo. «Y perseverando unánimes cada día en el templo» (Hechos 2:46). «Todos perseveraban unánimes en oración» (Hechos 1:14). Los creyentes se reunían con una atmósfera. La gente entraba de las calles y sentía la atmósfera antes de jamás oír un sermón. «Y de los demás, ninguno se atrevía a juntarse con ellos; mas el pueblo los alababa grandemente» (Hechos 5:13). Aun los incrédulos podían sentir la diferencia entre ese cuarto y cualquier otro cuarto en Jerusalén.

blocks.en: The Christian Education teacher cultivates that atmosphere by personally being warm before he is informative. The lesson can be repeated. The first impression of warmth cannot. A teacher who greets every learner by name at the door, who notices the absent and asks about them, who treats every question as worthy of an answer, has built an atmosphere that no curriculum could buy.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro de Educación Cristiana cultiva esa atmósfera siendo personalmente cálido antes de ser informativo. La lección puede repetirse. La primera impresión de calidez no puede. Un maestro que saluda a cada aprendiz por nombre en la puerta, que nota a los ausentes y pregunta por ellos, que trata cada pregunta como digna de una respuesta, ha construido una atmósfera que ningún currículo podría comprar.

blocks.en: IV. The Spiritual Environment: The Shaken Room
blocks.es_reference: IV. El ambiente espiritual: El cuarto sacudido

blocks.en: The most powerful environment in any Christian Education classroom is invisible. It is the presence of God Himself. A classroom where God's presence is welcomed will hold and shape its learners in ways no classroom techniques can match. A classroom where God's presence is forgotten will, over time, feel like any other classroom on earth.
blocks.es_reference: El ambiente más poderoso en cualquier aula de Educación Cristiana es invisible. Es la presencia de Dios mismo. Un aula donde se da la bienvenida a la presencia de Dios sostendrá y moldeará a sus aprendices de maneras que ninguna técnica de aula puede igualar. Un aula donde la presencia de Dios es olvidada, con el tiempo, se sentirá como cualquier otra aula en la tierra.

blocks.en: Acts 4 gives a glimpse of what spiritual environment looks like at full strength. The disciples had just been threatened by the Jewish leaders and forbidden to preach in the name of Jesus. They returned to their company and prayed. The text says, "And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together; and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness" (Acts 4:31).
blocks.es_reference: Hechos 4 da un vistazo de cómo se ve el ambiente espiritual en plena fuerza. Los discípulos acababan de ser amenazados por los líderes judíos y se les había prohibido predicar en el nombre de Jesús. Volvieron a su compañía y oraron. El texto dice: «Y cuando hubieron orado, el lugar en que estaban congregados tembló; y todos fueron llenos del Espíritu Santo, y hablaban con denuedo la palabra de Dios» (Hechos 4:31).

blocks.en: The room itself shook. That is rare. But the principle behind the shaking is not rare at all. When God's people pray, God shows up. When God shows up, the room is changed. When the room is changed, the learners are changed.
blocks.es_reference: El cuarto mismo tembló. Eso es raro. Pero el principio detrás del temblor no es raro en absoluto. Cuando el pueblo de Dios ora, Dios se presenta. Cuando Dios se presenta, el cuarto cambia. Cuando el cuarto cambia, los aprendices cambian.

blocks.en: The Christian Education teacher prepares the spiritual environment in three quiet ways. First, the teacher prays in the room before the learners arrive — a habit so simple and so powerful that a thousand teachers across history have walked into their empty classroom on Saturday night just to pray over the empty chairs. Second, the teacher prays in the room when class begins, briefly and sincerely, leading the learners to invite the One who is already there. Third, the teacher prays for the learners by name during the week, so that on Sunday morning the prayer carries a face and not a slot.
blocks.es_reference: El maestro de Educación Cristiana prepara el ambiente espiritual en tres maneras silenciosas. Primero, el maestro ora en el cuarto antes de que los aprendices lleguen — un hábito tan simple y tan poderoso que mil maestros a través de la historia han entrado a su aula vacía el sábado por la noche sólo para orar sobre las sillas vacías. Segundo, el maestro ora en el cuarto cuando la clase comienza, brevemente y sinceramente, guiando a los aprendices a invitar a Aquel que ya está ahí. Tercero, el maestro ora por los aprendices por nombre durante la semana, para que el domingo por la mañana la oración cargue un rostro y no un puesto.

blocks.en: A room prayed over feels different. A room never prayed over feels different too, and the learners feel the difference even if they cannot name it. The teacher who skips this step is teaching in his own strength alone, and his own strength is not enough.
blocks.es_reference: Un cuarto sobre el cual se ha orado se siente diferente. Un cuarto sobre el cual nunca se ha orado se siente diferente también, y los aprendices sienten la diferencia aunque no puedan nombrarla. El maestro que se salta este paso está enseñando en su propia fuerza solamente, y su propia fuerza no es suficiente.

blocks.en: V. The Battle Against Distractions
blocks.es_reference: V. La batalla contra las distracciones

blocks.en: Every classroom has distractions. The teacher who pretends otherwise will lose every battle. The teacher who plans for distractions will win most of them.
blocks.es_reference: Cada aula tiene distracciones. El maestro que pretende lo contrario perderá cada batalla. El maestro que planea para las distracciones ganará la mayoría de ellas.

blocks.en: Distractions are of three kinds. There are external distractions: noise from the hallway, traffic outside, a phone ringing in the next room, the smell of coffee from the fellowship hall. There are internal distractions: a learner who came worried about a sick parent, a teenager whose mind is on a Friday-night fight, a five-year-old who skipped his nap. And there are environmental distractions: the broken light flickering overhead, the chair that squeaks every time someone shifts, the printed handout with the typo that gets passed around.
blocks.es_reference: Las distracciones son de tres clases. Hay distracciones externas: ruido del pasillo, tráfico afuera, un teléfono sonando en el cuarto de al lado, el olor del café del salón de comunión. Hay distracciones internas: un aprendiz que vino preocupado por un padre enfermo, un adolescente cuya mente está en una pelea del viernes por la noche, un niño de cinco años que se saltó su siesta. Y hay distracciones ambientales: la luz rota parpadeando arriba, la silla que cruje cada vez que alguien se mueve, el folleto impreso con el error tipográfico que se pasa de mano en mano.

blocks.en: External distractions are managed by environment. Close the door. Move the class to a quieter room when possible. Ask the kitchen helpers to keep the door of the fellowship hall closed during the lesson. Eliminate what can be eliminated; absorb what cannot.
blocks.es_reference: Las distracciones externas se manejan por ambiente. Cierre la puerta. Mueva la clase a un cuarto más quieto cuando sea posible. Pídale a los ayudantes de cocina que mantengan cerrada la puerta del salón de comunión durante la lección. Elimine lo que se puede eliminar; absorba lo que no.

blocks.en: Internal distractions are managed by relationship. The teacher who knows his learners can sometimes tell, in the first minute, that a learner is carrying something heavy. A quiet word at the door — "How are you doing today, really?" — can sometimes lift the weight enough that the learner can hear the lesson. If not, the teacher does not insist on the lesson plan; he meets the need. The lesson plan can wait. The hurting learner cannot.
blocks.es_reference: Las distracciones internas se manejan por relación. El maestro que conoce a sus aprendices puede a veces decir, en el primer minuto, que un aprendiz está cargando algo pesado. Una palabra silenciosa en la puerta — «¿Cómo estás hoy, de verdad?» — puede a veces levantar el peso lo suficiente para que el aprendiz pueda oír la lección. Si no, el maestro no insiste en el plan de lección; suple la necesidad. El plan de lección puede esperar. El aprendiz herido no puede.

blocks.en: Environmental distractions are managed by preparation. Replace the bulb. Tighten the chair. Proofread the handout. The hour spent on Saturday is the hour saved on Sunday. Most environmental distractions are entirely preventable, and a teacher who keeps allowing the same flickering light to interrupt the same lesson week after week is teaching the learners that the lesson is not very important to the teacher either.
blocks.es_reference: Las distracciones ambientales se manejan por preparación. Reemplace el bombillo. Apriete la silla. Revise el folleto. La hora gastada el sábado es la hora ahorrada el domingo. La mayoría de las distracciones ambientales son enteramente prevenibles, y un maestro que sigue permitiendo que la misma luz parpadeante interrumpa la misma lección semana tras semana les está enseñando a los aprendices que la lección tampoco es muy importante para el maestro.

blocks.en: VI. The Teacher's Preparation: The Saturday Night
blocks.es_reference: VI. La preparación del maestro: La noche del sábado

blocks.en: The preparation of the environment happens the day before the class meets, not the morning of. Mark 14 tells us that Jesus sent two disciples ahead of the Passover meal with detailed instructions. They were to find a man with a pitcher of water, follow him, ask the master of the house for the guestchamber, and there "he will show you a large upper room, furnished and prepared; there make ready for us" (Mark 14:15). Notice the words: furnished and prepared. The room was already cared for before the disciples arrived. They added to what was already there.
blocks.es_reference: La preparación del ambiente sucede el día antes de que la clase se reúna, no la mañana misma. Marcos 14 nos dice que Jesús envió a dos discípulos por adelantado a la comida de la Pascua con instrucciones detalladas. Debían encontrar un hombre con un cántaro de agua, seguirlo, pedirle al señor de la casa el aposento, y allí «él os mostrará un gran aposento alto ya dispuesto; preparad para nosotros allí» (Marcos 14:15). Note las palabras: ya dispuesto. El cuarto ya había sido cuidado antes de que los discípulos llegaran. Ellos añadieron a lo que ya estaba ahí.

blocks.en: The Christian Education teacher's Saturday is the equivalent. Saturday afternoon or evening, the teacher walks into the empty classroom. He arranges the chairs. He sets out the supplies. He checks the lighting. He makes the room beautiful, even by a little. He prays. He thinks through the lesson once more, in the room where it will be taught. And he leaves.
blocks.es_reference: El sábado del maestro de Educación Cristiana es el equivalente. El sábado por la tarde o por la noche, el maestro entra al aula vacía. Arregla las sillas. Saca los materiales. Revisa la iluminación. Hace el cuarto hermoso, aun un poquito. Ora. Repasa la lección una vez más, en el cuarto donde será enseñada. Y se va.

blocks.en: When the learners walk in on Sunday morning, they walk into a room that has already been prepared for them. They do not know how. They cannot say what is different. But they feel it. The lesson begins before the bell rings.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando los aprendices entran el domingo por la mañana, entran a un cuarto que ya ha sido preparado para ellos. No saben cómo. No pueden decir qué es diferente. Pero lo sienten. La lección comienza antes de que suene el timbre.

blocks.en: A teacher who prepares the environment on Saturday teaches a different lesson on Sunday than a teacher who arrives at five minutes to nine and starts shoving chairs. Same lesson plan. Same Bible. Different atmosphere. Different result. The Saturday investment is the smallest, quietest, most consistently underrated tool the Christian Education teacher has at his disposal.
blocks.es_reference: Un maestro que prepara el ambiente el sábado enseña una lección diferente el domingo que un maestro que llega cinco minutos antes de las nueve y empieza a empujar sillas. El mismo plan de lección. La misma Biblia. Atmósfera diferente. Resultado diferente. La inversión del sábado es la herramienta más pequeña, más silenciosa, más consistentemente subestimada que el maestro de Educación Cristiana tiene a su disposición.

blocks.en: Closing: A Large Upper Room Furnished and Prepared
blocks.es_reference: Cierre: Un gran aposento alto ya dispuesto

blocks.en: The phrase from Mark 14:15 is one of the most quietly beautiful pictures of Christian Education in the Gospels. The Master Teacher sent disciples ahead to a room that was already furnished and prepared. Someone had cared for that room before the Lord ever needed it. Someone had made it ready.
blocks.es_reference: La frase de Marcos 14:15 es una de las imágenes más silenciosamente hermosas de la Educación Cristiana en los Evangelios. El Maestro de Maestros envió discípulos por adelantado a un cuarto que estaba ya dispuesto. Alguien había cuidado ese cuarto antes de que el Señor lo necesitara. Alguien lo había preparado.

blocks.en: That is what the Christian Education teacher does for his classroom every week. He furnishes it. He prepares it. He makes it ready, so that when the learners walk in, what they encounter is not chaos but care, not improvisation but invitation. The room itself preaches a small sermon before the teacher opens his mouth: "You were expected. We made it ready for you."
blocks.es_reference: Eso es lo que el maestro de Educación Cristiana hace por su aula cada semana. La amuebla. La prepara. La deja lista, para que cuando los aprendices entren, lo que encuentren no sea caos sino cuidado, no improvisación sino invitación. El cuarto mismo predica un pequeño sermón antes de que el maestro abra la boca: «Te estábamos esperando. La preparamos para ti».

blocks.en: Three environments — physical, emotional, spiritual — wrap around every classroom. The teacher who attends to all three has prepared the field. The seed will fall on soil that has been broken, watered, and warmed. The harvest is the LORD's, but the field is the teacher's responsibility.
blocks.es_reference: Tres ambientes — físico, emocional, espiritual — envuelven cada aula. El maestro que atiende los tres ha preparado el campo. La semilla caerá sobre tierra que ha sido quebrada, regada, y calentada. La cosecha es del Señor, pero el campo es la responsabilidad del maestro.

blocks.en: In Unit 6 we will turn from the place to the lesson itself. We will look at how a clear teaching aim turns a forty-minute hour from a wandering walk into a planned journey, and how a written lesson plan becomes the trail the teacher follows so that, at the end of the class, the learners are exactly where the teacher hoped they would be.
blocks.es_reference: En la Unidad 6 nos volveremos del lugar a la lección misma. Veremos cómo un objetivo de enseñanza claro convierte una hora de cuarenta minutos de una caminata errante a un viaje planeado, y cómo un plan de lección escrito se convierte en el sendero que el maestro sigue para que, al final de la clase, los aprendices estén exactamente donde el maestro esperaba que estuvieran.

mc.stem: What is the anchor scripture for Unit 5?
mc.why: Mark 14:15 anchors this unit. The Master Teacher Himself sent two disciples ahead to prepare the room where the most important teaching meal in history would be eaten. The phrase 'furnished and prepared' captures the heart of environmental preparation.

mc.stem: What three environments wrap around every Christian Education classroom?
mc.why: Andi names three environments: the physical (the room itself), the emotional (the atmosphere), and the spiritual (the presence of God). The teacher who attends to all three has somewhere for the lesson to land.

mc.stem: From where did Jesus teach in Mark 4 when the crowd grew too large?
options: A boat pushed out from shore
mc.why: Mark 4:1. Jesus stepped into a boat and sat in the sea while the crowd stood on the shore. The lake became a natural amphitheater, the water carried his voice, and every face had a clear view. The Master Teacher chose his physical environment.

mc.stem: What does Jesus's choice of the boat in Mark 4 illustrate?
options: That a master teacher chooses his physical environment
That he wanted to escape the crowd
That he was tired of teaching
mc.why: Jesus optimized the conditions: voice carried by water, clear sight lines, room for thousands. The Christian Education teacher does the same with his classroom — lighting, seating, cleanliness, supplies — because every physical detail is part of the lesson.

mc.stem: Which is NOT one of the physical environment elements Andi names?
options: Comfortable temperature and seating that fits
Visibility, quiet, and supplies within reach
mc.why: Andi's list is concrete and practical: cleanliness, brightness, comfortable temperature, seating that fits, visibility, quiet, supplies ready and within reach. None of it glamorous; all of it matters.

mc.stem: Where did Paul teach daily in Ephesus for two years (Acts 19)?
mc.why: Acts 19:9. After three months in the synagogue, Paul rented Tyrannus's school. He taught daily for two years. Fixed place, fixed time, sustained over time — the result was that all who dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus.

mc.stem: How long did Paul's teaching at the school of Tyrannus continue?
mc.why: Acts 19:10 says 'this continued by the space of two years.' Same place, same hour, day after day, for twenty-four months. Predictability is itself an environment.

mc.stem: What was the result of Paul's two years of daily teaching at Tyrannus?
options: All they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus
He was forced to leave Ephesus
mc.why: Acts 19:10. One classroom changed a province. Sustained, predictable teaching in a fixed place reaches farther than dramatic crusades. The Christian Education classroom needs the same kind of dependable schedule.

mc.stem: What three questions does the atmosphere answer for the learner before he sits down?
options: Where do I sit? When do we eat? Who is teaching?
Am I welcome here? Is it safe to ask anything? Will I be valued whether I know the right answer or not?
Did I bring my Bible? Is there a quiz? Where is the bathroom?
What's the offering? Will I be called on? When does it end?
mc.why: If the atmosphere answers yes to those three questions, the learner returns even after an uneven lesson. If it answers no, the learner does not return even after an excellent lesson. The teacher answers them with eyes, with names, with patience.

mc.stem: What is the Greek word Luke uses repeatedly to describe the early church's gatherings?
mc.why: Homothumadon means 'with one mind, in one mood.' Acts 1:14, 2:46, and elsewhere describe the believers meeting with one accord. People walked in from the streets and felt the atmosphere before any sermon was preached.

mc.stem: What happened to the place where the disciples were assembled when they prayed (Acts 4:31)?
options: It was shaken; they were filled with the Holy Ghost; they spake the word of God with boldness
mc.why: Acts 4:31. The room itself shook. The principle is not the shaking but the cause: when God's people pray, God shows up; when God shows up, the room is changed; when the room is changed, the learners are changed.

mc.stem: Which is NOT one of the three quiet ways Andi says the teacher prepares the spiritual environment?
options: Praying in the room before the learners arrive
Leading a brief sincere opening prayer with the learners
Praying for the learners by name during the week
Posting a Scripture verse on every wall of the room
mc.why: The three Andi names are praying alone in the room beforehand, leading a sincere opening prayer, and praying for learners by name during the week. Wall verses are not wrong; they are simply not what makes a room feel prayed-over.

mc.stem: What three kinds of distractions does Andi name?
mc.why: External (hallway noise, traffic), internal (a worried learner, a tired five-year-old), and environmental (flickering lights, squeaky chairs, typo-ridden handouts). Each kind is managed in a different way.

mc.stem: How are external distractions best managed?
options: By turning up the teacher's voice
By environment — close doors, move rooms when possible, eliminate what can be eliminated
mc.why: External distractions are managed by environmental controls. Eliminate what can be eliminated; absorb what cannot. Closing the door is sometimes the most spiritual act of the morning.

mc.stem: How are internal distractions (a learner carrying a heavy burden) best managed?
options: By relationship — a quiet word at the door, sometimes setting aside the lesson plan
mc.why: Internal distractions are managed by relationship. The teacher who knows his learners can sometimes lift the weight with a quiet word at the door. The lesson plan can wait; the hurting learner cannot.

mc.stem: How are environmental distractions (a flickering bulb, a squeaky chair) best managed?
options: By preparation — replace the bulb, tighten the chair, proofread the handout
By raising the volume of teaching
mc.why: Most environmental distractions are entirely preventable. The hour spent on Saturday is the hour saved on Sunday. A teacher who keeps allowing the same flickering light to interrupt week after week teaches the learners that the lesson is not very important to him either.

mc.stem: What two-word phrase from Mark 14:15 describes the upper room?
mc.why: 'A large upper room furnished and prepared.' The room was already cared for before the disciples arrived; they added to what was already there. That is the picture of the teacher's Saturday preparation.

mc.stem: When should the teacher's preparation of the room happen?
options: The day before — Saturday afternoon or evening
mc.why: Preparation happens the day before, not the morning of. Saturday afternoon or evening, the teacher arranges chairs, sets supplies, prays, and walks through the lesson in the room. Sunday morning, he arrives early, not panicking.

mc.stem: What sermon does the prepared room preach to the learners before the teacher opens his mouth?
options: "You were expected. We made it ready for you."
"This is going to be a long lesson"
mc.why: The prepared room preaches care, invitation, and expectation before any words are spoken. Learners feel it even when they cannot name it. A room never prepared preaches the opposite sermon, and learners feel that too.

mc.stem: What does Unit 6 cover, according to the closing of Unit 5?
options: Teaching aims and the lesson plan
mc.why: Unit 6 turns from the place to the lesson itself. A clear teaching aim turns a forty-minute hour from a wandering walk into a planned journey. A written lesson plan becomes the trail the teacher follows so that, at the end of the class, the learners are exactly where the teacher hoped they would be.
